## Prerequisites

- Hardware: one Atlas A2 64 GB NPU.
- Weights: BF16, downloaded from ModelScope.
- Download the weights to a directory accessible from the deployment environment. For multi-node deployment, use a shared directory; for example, `/root/.cache/`.

## Installation

Use the vLLM-Ascend Docker image that corresponds to your hardware. Replace the model weight mount path with the path used in your environment.

```bash
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0

docker run --rm \
    --name vllm-ascend \
    --shm-size=1g \
    --net host \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/devmm_svm \
    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64 \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
    -it -d $IMAGE bash
```

## Deployment

```shell
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
export TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1

vllm serve /data/llm-workspace/cohere-transcribe-03-2026 \
  --served-model-name cohere-transcribe \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --block-size 128 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000
```

## Verification

Verify that the container is running and that the installed package versions match the image tag:

```bash
docker ps --filter name=vllm-ascend
pip show vllm vllm-ascend
```

Expected result: `docker ps` lists the container with status `Up`, and `pip show` displays the version information of both packages.

> Source: https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/zh-cn/v0.30.0/tutorials/models/Cohere-Transcribe.html (v0.30.0, Atlas A2 inference product tab)

guideMd:
## Prerequisites

### Model Weights

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | Download Links |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 |  | ModelScope |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | 1 950DT node (96GB × 8) | Hugging Face |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8 | Ascend 950PR & 950DT series products | Quantized locally with msmodelslim |

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8` (W4A4 MXFP4 mixed-precision quantization): For how ultra-low-bit quantization preserves accuracy, see [W4A4C8 FAQs](#q-how-do-the-w4a4c8-ultra-low-bit-quantized-weights-preserve-accuracy).

It is recommended to download the model weights to a shared directory for multiple nodes, for example `/root/.cache/`.

**Path note**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record the path. Make sure that the model path in the subsequent deployment commands matches this directory.

### Verify Multi-Node Communication (Optional)

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to verify multi-node communication according to [Verify the multi-node communication environment](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

## Installation

Select the image according to your machine type and start the Docker image on your node; see [Using Docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image).

Start a Docker container on each server.

```bash
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a5
export NAME=vllm-ascend
docker run --rm \
    --name $NAME \
    --net=host \
    --shm-size=512g \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci1 \
    --device /dev/davinci2 \
    --device /dev/davinci3 \
    --device /dev/davinci4 \
    --device /dev/davinci5 \
    --device /dev/davinci6 \
    --device /dev/davinci7 \
    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    --device /dev/ummu \
    --device /dev/uburma \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
    -v /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/sbin \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/sbin/npu-smi:/usr/local/sbin/npu-smi \
    -itd $IMAGE bash
```

After Docker runs successfully, you can run the `docker ps` command to verify that the container service is running properly.

## Deployment

###

Note

In this tutorial, we assume that you have downloaded the model weights to `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/`. You can change it to your own path as needed.

It is recommended to wrap the following service code in a .sh script file and execute it in Bash mode.

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-machine deployment completes Prefill and Decode within the same node.

Run the following script to perform online inference with mixed PD deployment.

```shell
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export OMP_PROC_BIND=false
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=CCU_SCHED
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1

vllm serve /root/.cache/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731  \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name dsv4 \
    --data-parallel-size 8 \
    --prefill-context-parallel-size 1 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --enable-chunked-prefill \
    --max-model-len 1048576 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --block-size 32 \
    --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
    --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark"}' \
    --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":"True","multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true,"enable_shared_expert_dp":true}' \
```

Key parameter descriptions:

`--max-model-len` specifies the maximum context length, that is, the sum of the input tokens and output tokens of a single request. Adjust it according to the actual scenario.

`--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of requests that each DP group can process. If the number of requests sent to the service exceeds this limit, the excess requests remain in the waiting state and are not scheduled. Note that the time spent in the waiting state is also counted in metrics such as TTFT and TPOT. Therefore, when testing performance, it is usually recommended that `--max-num-seqs` * `--data-parallel-size` >= the actual total concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in a single scheduling step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--data-parallel-size` sets the number of global data parallel ranks, while `--tensor-parallel-size` sets the tensor parallel size within each DP rank. Configure them together according to the deployment topology and available NPUs.

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--no-enable-prefix-caching` disables prefix caching. To enable it, remove this option.

`--block-size` sets the KV cache block size. To enable the experimental 4k prefix cache hit support, change it from `128` to `32`.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for W8A8 models.

`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` enables 4-bit TurboQuant quantization for the Compress-4 attention KV cache of DeepSeek-V4 to reduce memory usage. It is suitable for ultra-long-context workloads such as AI coding, especially when KV cache memory limits concurrency. It is independent of weight and indexer cache quantization and requires compatible TurboQuant and fused attention operators. PD-disaggregated deployment is not currently supported.

`--speculative-config` configures speculative decoding to accelerate inference. For DSpark models, use `dspark`. When using DSpark, `num_speculative_tokens` must be at least 5 (see the checkpoint's `config.json`).

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full ACL graph execution during decoding to reduce scheduling latency.

`--additional-config` enables Ascend-specific optimizations. `enable_npugraph_ex` enables enhanced ACL graph execution, `enable_static_kernel: false` keeps static kernel compilation disabled, `enable_cpu_binding` enables Ascend-native CPU binding, and `multistream_overlap_shared_expert` overlaps shared expert computation for better MoE throughput.

FAQ tip: If you encounter problems, refer to the [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) for troubleshooting.

Service verification: Use the API port configured for the selected deployment. For the 950DT example, use port `8000`.

```shell
curl http://<node0_ip>:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "dsv4",
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": "Who are you?"
            }
        ],
        "max_tokens": 256,
        "temperature": 0
    }'
```

Expected result:

The service returns HTTP 200 OK, and the JSON response contains the `choices` field.

## Verification

This section verifies the basic inference function of all deployment modes. For Memcache pooled PD deployment, verify external KV Cache Pool reuse by following the "Start the proxy and verify KV Cache Pool reuse" step in the [verification steps](#534-startup-and-verification) or the [950DT example](#54-950dt-single-node-pd-separation-deployment).

After the server is started, you can query the model with an input prompt:

For the single-node deployment in Section 5.1, replace `<node0_ip>` and `<port>` with the IP address and port of the API server. For the PD-disaggregated deployment in Section 5.2 or the KV Cache Pool deployment in Section 5.3, use the IP address and port of the proxy, because requests are routed through the proxy to the Prefill and Decode instances.

```shell
curl http://<node0_ip>:<port>/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "dsv4",
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": "Who are you?"
            }
        ],
        "max_tokens": 256,
        "temperature": 0
    }'
```

Expected result:

The service returns HTTP 200 OK, and the JSON response contains the `choices` field.

```shell
      "pp_size": 1,
      "pcp_size": 1
    }
  },
  "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail"
}'

  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port "$((7100 + p_rank))" \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --data-parallel-rank "$p_rank" \

  --api-server-count 4 \
  --block-size 32 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.96 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --enforce-eager \
  --quantization ascend \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype int8 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --seed 1024 \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":true,"num_threads":128}' \
```

```shell
    --data-parallel-rpc-port 12321 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --seed 1024 \
    --max-model-len 508576 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 720 \
    --max-num-seqs 128 \
    --async-scheduling \
    --block-size 32 \
    --served-model-name dsv4 \
    --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype int8 \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
    --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":true,"num_threads":128}' \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 \
    --quantization ascend \
    --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":1,"method":"dspark"}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --kv-transfer-config "$kv_config" \
    --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config":{"enable_npugraph_ex":true,"enable_static_kernel":false},"enable_cpu_binding":true,"multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true,"recompute_scheduler_enable":true}' &

```

Start the proxy: replace `p_a`, `p_b`, and the IPs of the Decode nodes with the actual addresses.

```shell
set -euo pipefail
proxy_workers=4
ulimit -n 65536
p_a="<PREFILL_NODE_A_IP>"
p_b="<PREFILL_NODE_B_IP>"
d_a="<DECODE_NODE_A_IP>"
d_b="<DECODE_NODE_B_IP>"
decode_hosts=()
decode_ports=()
for node in "$d_a" "$d_b"; do
  for port in 7100 7101 7102 7103 7104 7105 7106 7107; do
    decode_hosts+=("$node")
    decode_ports+=("$port")
  done
done
python3 examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 18590 \
  --workers "$proxy_workers" \
  --prefiller-hosts "$p_a" "$p_b" \
  --prefiller-ports 7100 7101 \
  --decoder-hosts "${decode_hosts[@]}" \
  --decoder-ports "${decode_ports[@]}"
```

guideMd:
## Prerequisites

- Hardware: Ascend 950DT series products, multi-node deployment.
- Weights: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, downloaded from Hugging Face; these weights already include the DSpark draft parameters.
- Quantization: MXFP8 for Attention and MXFP4 (W4A8) for MoE, with no Ascend-specific quantization or weight conversion required.
- Path: Download the weights to a multi-node shared directory (for example `/root/.cache/`), consistent with the path in the deployment commands.
- Network: Verify inter-node communication before deploying across multiple nodes.

## Installation

Start the container (Ascend 950DT series); adjust `--device` and `-v` according to the actual number of cards and the weight path:

```bash
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a5
export NAME=vllm-ascend

docker run --rm \
    --name $NAME \
    --net=host \
    --shm-size=512g \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci1 \
    --device /dev/davinci2 \
    --device /dev/davinci3 \
    --device /dev/davinci4 \
    --device /dev/davinci5 \
    --device /dev/davinci6 \
    --device /dev/davinci7 \
    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    --device /dev/ummu \
    --device /dev/uburma \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /etc/hccl_rootinfo.json:/etc/hccl_rootinfo.json \
    -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
    -v /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/sbin \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/sbin/npu-smi:/usr/local/sbin/npu-smi \
    -itd $IMAGE bash
```

## Deployment

Start the service on the first node and on the remaining nodes respectively (the same set of commands, with roles distinguished by environment variables):

```bash
# nic_name is the network interface that owns local_ip on the current node.
nic_name="xxx"
local_ip="xxx"

# node0_ip must be the local_ip of Node0 on every node.
node0_ip="xxxx"

export HCCL_IF_IP=$local_ip
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name
export TP_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024

export OMP_PROC_BIND=false
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=CCU_SCHED
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1

export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3000
export HCCL_EXEC_TIMEOUT=2040
export HCCL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=1200

export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1

vllm serve /root/.cache/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --served-model-name dsv4 \
    --port 8000 \
    --data-parallel-size 2 \
    --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
    --data-parallel-address $node0_ip \
    --data-parallel-rpc-port 6987 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --prefill-context-parallel-size 8 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --seed 1024 \
    --max-model-len 1048576 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
    --max-num-seqs 16 \
    --async-scheduling \
    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
    --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":true,"num_threads":128}' \
    --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark"}' \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --block-size 32 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --additional-config '{
      "ascend_compilation_config":{
        "enable_npugraph_ex":true,
        "enable_static_kernel":false
      },
      "enable_cpu_binding":true,
      "enable_fused_mc2":0,
      "enable_shared_expert_dp":true,
      "multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true
    }'
```

## Prerequisites

- Hardware: The A2 series 1P1D deployment uses four Atlas 800I A2 servers, each with 8 NPUs and 64GB per NPU, and exposes 8 devices to the container.
- Weights: A2 uses the `Eco-Tech/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-w8a8` (ModelScope) checkpoint, which contains the DSpark draft parameters and the INT8 Engram table.
- Path: Download the checkpoint to the same absolute path on each server, and replace `<YOUR_MODEL_PATH>` in the service commands with that directory.
- Version: This guide is written and verified based on vLLM v0.30.0 and vLLM Ascend v0.30.0.

## Installation

Start the A2 series Docker container: if the weights are stored elsewhere, modify `MODEL_ROOT`, and ensure the same absolute path is used inside and outside the container.

```shell
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0
export MODEL_ROOT="/data/weights"

docker pull "$IMAGE"

docker run --rm -it \
  --name deepseek-v41 \
  --net=host \
  --shm-size=512g \
  --privileged=true \
  --device /dev/davinci0 \
  --device /dev/davinci1 \
  --device /dev/davinci2 \
  --device /dev/davinci3 \

  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool \
  -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
  -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
  -v /etc/hccn.conf:/etc/hccn.conf \
  -v "$MODEL_ROOT:$MODEL_ROOT" \
  "$IMAGE" bash
```

## Deployment

Save the `launch_online_dp.py` launcher, which is shared by the three hardware tabs.

```python
import argparse
import multiprocessing
import os
import subprocess
import sys

def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--dp-size", type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--tp-size", type=int, default=1)
    parser.add_argument("--dp-size-local", type=int, default=-1)
    parser.add_argument("--dp-rank-start", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--dp-address", type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--dp-rpc-port", type=str, default="12345")
    parser.add_argument("--vllm-start-port", type=int, default=9000)
    return parser.parse_args()

args = parse_args()
dp_size = args.dp_size
tp_size = args.tp_size
dp_size_local = args.dp_size if args.dp_size_local == -1 else args.dp_size_local

def run_command(visible_devices, dp_rank, vllm_engine_port):
    command = [
        "bash",
        "./run_dp_template.sh",
        visible_devices,
        str(vllm_engine_port),
        str(dp_size),
        str(dp_rank),
        args.dp_address,
        args.dp_rpc_port,
        str(tp_size),
    ]
    subprocess.run(command, check=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if not os.path.exists("./run_dp_template.sh"):
        print("Template file ./run_dp_template.sh does not exist.")
        sys.exit(1)

    processes = []
    for i in range(dp_size_local):
        dp_rank = args.dp_rank_start + i
        vllm_engine_port = args.vllm_start_port + i
        visible_devices = ",".join(
            str(device) for device in range(i * tp_size, (i + 1) * tp_size)
        )
        process = multiprocessing.Process(
            target=run_command,
            args=(visible_devices, dp_rank, vllm_engine_port),
        )
        processes.append(process)
        process.start()

    for process in processes:
        process.join()
```

## Deployment

Save the launcher script as `launch_online_dp.py` on both nodes; it assigns the devices visible to the node to local DP ranks and starts one vLLM process for each rank.

```python
import argparse
import multiprocessing
import os
import subprocess
import sys

def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--dp-size", type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--tp-size", type=int, default=1)
    parser.add_argument("--dp-size-local", type=int, default=-1)
    parser.add_argument("--dp-rank-start", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--dp-address", type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--dp-rpc-port", type=str, default="12345")
    parser.add_argument("--vllm-start-port", type=int, default=9000)
    return parser.parse_args()

args = parse_args()
dp_size = args.dp_size
tp_size = args.tp_size
dp_size_local = args.dp_size if args.dp_size_local == -1 else args.dp_size_local

def run_command(visible_devices, dp_rank, vllm_engine_port):
    command = [
        "bash",
        "./run_dp_template.sh",
        visible_devices,
        str(vllm_engine_port),
        str(dp_size),
        str(dp_rank),
        args.dp_address,
        args.dp_rpc_port,
        str(tp_size),
    ]
    subprocess.run(command, check=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if not os.path.exists("./run_dp_template.sh"):
        print("Template file ./run_dp_template.sh does not exist.")
        sys.exit(1)

    processes = []
    for i in range(dp_size_local):
        dp_rank = args.dp_rank_start + i
        vllm_engine_port = args.vllm_start_port + i
        visible_devices = ",".join(
            str(device) for device in range(i * tp_size, (i + 1) * tp_size)
        )
        process = multiprocessing.Process(
            target=run_command,
            args=(visible_devices, dp_rank, vllm_engine_port),
        )
        processes.append(process)
        process.start()

    for process in processes:
        process.join()
```

## Prerequisites

- Hardware: 2 Atlas 800 A2 (64GB × 8) servers, each with 8 NPUs, exposing 8 devices to the container.
- Weights: `GLM-5.1-w8a8` quantized version, downloaded from Modelers.
- Path: Download the weights to a shared directory for multiple nodes, for example `/root/.cache/`; both nodes use the same path.
- Network: Set `nic_name` to the NIC name found by `ifconfig`, `local_ip` to the IP of the current node, and `node0_ip` to the `local_ip` of node 0.
- Parallelism: `--data-parallel-size 2` and `--data-parallel-size-local 1`; node 1 carries `--headless` and a starting rank offset.

## Installation

Pull the image and start the container on each of the two nodes: `vllm-ascend` is the container name, and the shared weight directory is mounted at the actual path.

```shell

    --name vllm-ascend \
    --shm-size=1g \

    -it $IMAGE bash
```

Run the script on node 0: set `nic_name` to the NIC name obtained from `ifconfig` and `local_ip` to the IP of this node; the example model path is `GLM-5.1-w4a8`, and when using the W8A8 weights of this record, replace it with the directory containing `GLM-5.1-w8a8`.

## Prerequisites

### Model Weights

Download the weights from ModelScope according to the hardware in the following table. 950DT products use a different quantization format and must not be mixed. `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/<checkpoint-name>` in the script is the local mount path, not the download source. Preserve the case of the repository name when naming the local directory.

| Weights | Hardware | Deployment Mode | Download | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8-mxfp8 | Ascend 950DT series products (96GB × 8 per node) | Single-machine deployment uses 1 node; PD deployment uses 2 nodes | ModelScope | Supports the W8A8C8 configuration: C8 is dynamic KV-cache quantization. Set --kv-cache-dtype fp8 in the service command to enable the FP8 KV cache; no separate C8 weight file is required. |
| GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 |  | Single-machine deployment uses 1 node; PD deployment uses 2 nodes | ModelScope | Supports the W8A8C8 configuration: C8 is dynamic KV-cache quantization. Set --kv-cache-dtype int8 in the service command to enable the INT8 KV cache; no separate C8 weight file is required. |
| GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 |  | Co-deployment requires 2 nodes; PD deployment requires 4 nodes | ModelScope | / |

You can quantize the model directly with [msmodelslim](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msmodelslim).

The weight files linked above are already quantized and can be used for serving directly. To quantize by yourself, follow the installation and command examples in the [msModelSlim quantization guide](https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/en/mindstudio/2610/TITools/msModelSlim/docs/en/user_guide/feature_guide/quick_quantization_v1/usage.md), and select the configuration that matches the specific model and target hardware from the [model recipes](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msmodelslim/tree/master/lab_practice). Do not reuse the YAML files of other models.

It is recommended to download the model weights to a shared directory for multiple nodes, for example `/root/.cache/`

### Verify Multi-Node Communication (Optional)

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, verify it according to [Verify the multi-node communication environment](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

## Installation

Select the image for your hardware and start the container on each node. For details, see [Using Docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image).

Start a Docker container on each node.

```shell
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a5
export NAME=vllm-ascend

docker run --rm \
--name $NAME \
--net=host \
--shm-size=1g \
--device /dev/davinci0 \
--device /dev/davinci1 \
--device /dev/davinci2 \
--device /dev/davinci3 \
--device /dev/davinci4 \
--device /dev/davinci5 \
--device /dev/davinci6 \
--device /dev/davinci7 \
--device /dev/davinci_manager \
--device /dev/hisi_hdc \
--device /dev/ummu \
--device /dev/uburma \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver \
-v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
-v /etc/hccl_rootinfo.json:/etc/hccl_rootinfo.json \
-v /etc/hixlep/:/etc/hixlep/ \
-v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
-v /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/sbin \
-v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
-v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
-v /usr/bin/urma_admin:/usr/bin/urma_admin \
-v /lib/route.conf:/lib/route.conf \
-itd $IMAGE bash
```

## Deployment

###

Note

Do not set `enable_thinking: false` / `thinking: false` for GLM-5.3-Flash, otherwise the output quality may degrade.

**Common Parameter Descriptions**

The following definitions apply to the deployment scenarios in this chapter. Parameter values must follow the script for the selected hardware and role; hardware-specific values must not be mixed.

| Parameter | Meaning and Constraints |
|---|---|
| HCCL_BUFFSIZE | Size of the CANN/HCCL communication buffer in MB; a positive integer, with a documented default of 200. A larger buffer consumes more device memory and is multiplied by the number of communication domains. Keep the hardware/role-specific values in the examples and include this memory when planning KV cache capacity. For allocation details and version-specific limits, see the CANN HCCL reference documentation. |
| HCCL_IF_IP and socket interface related variables | Set the communication IP of the current node and the matching network interface. Peers must be able to reach it over the selected network. |
| --data-parallel-size, --tensor-parallel-size, --pipeline-parallel-size | DP is the number of data parallel ranks; TP and PP split each model engine across multiple devices and pipeline stages. Follow the topology and deployment mode in the selected tab. |
| --max-model-len | Upper limit of the total sequence length (in tokens), including the input and the generated output. Requests must satisfy this limit and the available KV cache capacity. |
| --max-num-seqs, --max-num-batched-tokens | Upper limits on the number of sequences and tokens processed by the scheduler in a single iteration, respectively. These limits apply per engine, not as a total limit at the proxy layer; tune them together with the context length and memory capacity. |
| --gpu-memory-utilization | Fraction of device memory allocated to the model executor. Although the parameter name contains gpu, it also applies to the NPU backend. Reserve space for communication buffers and other device allocations. |
| --quantization ascend | Selects the Ascend quantization loader for ModelSlim weights. Use weights that match the selected hardware and quantization format. |
| --kv-cache-dtype, --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype | Selects the KV cache format for attention and the indexer. Follow the examples for the selected weights and hardware; the formats supported differ across platforms. |
| --tool-call-parser glm47, --enable-auto-tool-choice | Parses tool calls and allows automatic tool selection. In PD deployment, it must be configured on both API service roles. |
| --reasoning-parser | Separates the reasoning process from the final answer. All examples on this page use glm47. |
| --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch | Reads weight files into the OS page cache before the worker loads them. This helps with network or high-latency storage and requires sufficient host memory; it does not preload weights into NPU memory. See the vLLM weight loading options. |

### Single-Node Online Deployment

#### Ascend 950DT series products[](#glm53-flash-5-1-950dt)

- The quantized model `GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8-mxfp8` can be deployed on 1 950DT products (96GB × 8) node.

Run the following script to perform online inference.

```shell
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024

vllm serve Eco-Tech/GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8-mxfp8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --served-model-name glm \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-model-len 132096 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1,2,4,8,16,32,64,96,128]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens": 3, "method": "deepseek_mtp", "enforce_eager": true}'
```

**Key Parameter Descriptions**

Only the key parameters specific to this model/scenario are described below. `max-model-len` and `max-num-seqs` need to be set according to the actual usage scenario.

**Model-specific parameters:**

`--data-parallel-size 1`: Runs one DP rank. `--tensor-parallel-size` is 8 on 950DT products to balance the memory capacity of the w8a8 weights against compute efficiency.

`--enable-expert-parallel`: This option must be enabled for the MoE architecture of GLM-5.3-Flash.

`--quantization ascend`: Enables Ascend quantization for the w8a8 quantized weights.

`--kv-cache-dtype`: Enables 8-bit KV cache quantization (C8) for sparse Flash Attention (SFA). C8 can be used when long contexts or concurrency are limited by KV cache memory. The complete single-node command above uses `fp8` on 950DT products. KV cache quantization is independent of weight quantization; enabling C8 does not require W8A8 weights or a separate C8 weight file.

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`: Enables graph capture only for the Decode phase, reducing kernel launch overhead to improve Decode performance.

`--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}'`: All deployment examples limit each prompt to at most one image and disable video input.

`--speculative-config`: Enables multi-token prediction (MTP) speculative decoding with the DeepSeek-style MTP draft head of GLM-5.3-Flash. The single-node example uses 3 speculative tokens on 950DT products. The `enforce_eager: true` setting on 950DT products keeps the draft model in eager mode. GLM-5.3-Flash supports MTP draft graph execution; the forced eager restriction of other GLM models does not apply to this model.

## Verification

After the selected deployment is ready, query its service endpoint. For Ascend 950DT series products PD deployment, use a separate proxy host and port `8000`.

```shell
curl http://<service_ip>:<service_port>/v1/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "glm",
        "prompt": "The future of AI is",
        "max_tokens": 50
    }'
```

Expected result: The response is a JSON payload containing the text generated by the model in text_completion format.

```json
{
  "id": "cmpl-123abc",
  "object": "text_completion",
  "created": 1725444000,
  "model": "glm",
  "choices": [
    {
      "text": " incredibly promising, with rapid advancements in machine learning and autonomous systems.",
      "index": 0,
      "finish_reason": "stop"
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 5,
    "completion_tokens": 15,
    "total_tokens": 20
  }
}
```

guideMd:
## Prerequisites

### Model Weights

Download the Gemma4 model weights to a local or shared directory, for example `/root/.cache/`. In the following examples, replace `/root/.cache/path/to/gemma4` with your actual model path.

| Weight Version | Description | Recommended Hardware | Download |
|---|---|---|---|
| google/gemma-4-31B-it | BF16 dense model. | Atlas 950PR & 950DT series products. Adjust the number of visible NPUs according to available memory. | ModelScope |
| Eco-Tech/gemma-4-31B-it-w4a4-mxfp4 | MXFP4 quantized dense model. | 1 Ascend 950DT series products (96GB × 8) node. | ModelScope |
| google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | BF16 MoE model, with about 26 billion total parameters and about 4 billion activated parameters. | Atlas 950PR & 950DT series products. Use tensor parallelism or expert parallelism according to the deployment scheme. | ModelScope |
| Eco-Tech/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-w4a4-mxfp4 | MXFP4 quantized MoE model. | 1 Ascend 950DT series products (96GB × 8) node. | ModelScope |

Both MXFP4 weights contain a `quant_model_description.json` file, and `--quantization ascend` must be specified when serving. For information about preparing quantized weights, see the [Quantization Guide](../../user_guide/feature_guide/quantization.html).

## Installation

Select the official all-in-one vLLM Ascend Docker image for your hardware. MXFP4 weights are supported on Ascend 950PR & 950DT series products

Gemma4 MXFP4 weights have been validated with this image. You can use this image or a later compatible v0.30.0 A5 image.

```shell
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a5
docker pull ${IMAGE}
```

Follow the hardware-specific `docker run` command in [Using prebuilt images](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image), and mount the directory containing the Gemma4 weights into the container. The prebuilt image contains matching CANN user-space environment, PyTorch, TorchNPU, vLLM, and vLLM Ascend versions.

After entering the container, verify the environment:

```shell
npu-smi info
python -m pip show vllm vllm-ascend
```

Expected result: `npu-smi info` lists the expected Ascend devices, and both Python packages are installed.

## Deployment

### Multi-Card Deployment

Example of single-machine multi-card deployment of Gemma4 on Ascend 950PR & 950DT series products. For different model sizes or device counts, adjust `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and `--tensor-parallel-size` according to the available NPUs.

## Verification

After the service is started, Gemma4 can be invoked through the OpenAI-compatible API.

### Completions API

```shell
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gemma4",
    "prompt": "Explain why graph execution improves decode performance.",
    "max_tokens": 128,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

### Chat Completions API

```shell
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gemma4",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Explain why graph execution improves decode performance."}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 128,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

Expected result: the request returns HTTP 200, and the JSON response contains the `choices` field, which contains the text generated by the model.

### Multimodal Chat Completions API

Send an image request to verify Gemma4 multimodal inference:

```shell
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gemma4",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
          {
            "type": "image_url",
            "image_url": {
              "url": "https://modelscope.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/resource/tiger.jpeg"
            }
          },
          {
            "type": "text",
            "text": "Describe this image."
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "max_tokens": 128,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

Expected result: the request returns HTTP 200, and the response describes the image in the `choices` field.

### Offline Inference

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="/root/.cache/path/to/gemma4",
    trust_remote_code=True,
    tensor_parallel_size=4,
    compilation_config={"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"},
)

sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=128)
outputs = llm.generate(
    ["Explain why graph execution improves decode performance."],
    sampling_params,
)

for output in outputs:
    print(output.outputs[0].text)
```

## Prerequisites

- Hardware: 1 Atlas 800I A2 (64GB × 8); adjust the number of visible NPUs for BF16 weights according to available memory.
- Weights: `google/gemma-4-31B-it` (BF16 dense) or `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (BF16 MoE), downloaded from ModelScope.
- Path: `/root/.cache/path/to/gemma4` in the examples is a placeholder and must be replaced with the actual weight directory.
- Version: vLLM-Ascend v0.30.0, image `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0`.
- Execution mode: Prefill and Decode are completed within a single node; the example uses 4 visible NPUs and TP4.

## Installation

Pull the official all-in-one image for this hardware; the image already contains matching CANN user-space environment, PyTorch, TorchNPU, vLLM, and vLLM Ascend versions.

```shell
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0
docker pull ${IMAGE}
```

After entering the container, check the devices and package versions.

```shell
npu-smi info
python -m pip show vllm vllm-ascend
```

Expected result: npu-smi info lists the expected Ascend devices, and both Python packages are installed.

## Deployment

Start the single-node online service in eager mode: set `MODEL_PATH` to the actual weight directory (replacing `/root/.cache/path/to/gemma4` in the example), and adjust `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and `--tensor-parallel-size` according to the actual number of NPUs.

```shell
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3

  --served-model-name gemma4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --enforce-eager
```

guideMd:
## Prerequisites

- Hardware: Atlas 300I DUO, TP2 deployment, using 2 cards.
- Weights: W8A8 quantized version, whose hardware requirement is Atlas 300I DUO (TP2), downloaded from ModelScope.
- Path: Replace `your_model_path` in the startup command with the downloaded weight directory.
- Image: `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-310p`, with vLLM and vLLM-Ascend already installed in the container.
- Parameters: W8A8 quantized models must keep `--quantization ascend`; adjust the other parameters according to the example and the actual devices.

## Installation

Start the container: the image is `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-310p`, the container name is `vllm-ascend`, and devices such as davinci0 and the driver paths are mapped.

```bash
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-310p

docker run --rm \
    --name vllm-ascend \
    --shm-size=1g \
    --net=host \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/devmm_svm \
    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
    -it $IMAGE bash
```

Confirm the vllm-ascend version inside the container.

```bash
pip show vllm-ascend
```

Expected result: the version information is displayed and matches the version of the pulled image.

## Deployment

Start the service on 300I DUO: replace `your_model_path` with the actual weight directory, `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1` are the chip IDs of the two cards, and adjust `--host 127.0.0.1` and `--port 8000` according to the actual environment.

```bash
export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
vllm serve your_model_path  \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --port 8000 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --served_model_name qwen3 \
    --dtype float16 \
    --quantization ascend \
    --max-model-len 16384 \
    --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config": {"fuse_norm_quant": false,"enable_npu_graph_ex":false}}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1,32]}' \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

| Parameter | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--tensor-parallel-size` | 2 | Maps the model onto two Atlas inference devices. Adjust it together with ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES according to the available devices and memory. |
| `--dtype` | float16 | Used for Atlas 300I DUO to match the Atlas inference execution path. |

## Verification

After the service is started, send a chat completion request: replace `localhost:8000` with the actual server IP and `--port` value, and `model` must match `--served-model-name`.

```shell
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "qwen3",
        "messages": [
            {"role": "user", "content": "Give me a short introduction to large language models."}
        ],
        "temperature": 0.6,
        "top_p": 0.95,
        "top_k": 20,
        "max_completion_tokens": 4096
    }'
```

Expected result: HTTP 200, returning a JSON response containing the `choices` field (with the generated text).

- Parameters: When using BF16 weights, remove `--quantization ascend` from the startup command.

## Installation

Start the container: the image is `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0`, the container name is `vllm-ascend-env`, and davinci0 through davinci7 and the driver paths are mapped.

```bash
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0

docker run \
    --name vllm-ascend-env \
    --ipc host \
    --net host \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci1 \
    --device /dev/davinci2 \
    --device /dev/davinci3 \
    --device /dev/davinci4 \
    --device /dev/davinci5 \
    --device /dev/davinci6 \
    --device /dev/davinci7 \
    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/devmm_svm \
    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/sbin \
    -it -d $IMAGE bash
```

Confirm that the container has started.

```bash
docker ps | grep vllm-ascend-env
```

Expected result: the container is listed with status `Up`.

## Deployment

Start the single-node online service: replace `your_model_path` with the actual weight directory, replace `your_eagle3_model_path` in `--speculative-config` with the draft model directory, remove `--quantization ascend` for BF16 weights, and adjust `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and `--tensor-parallel-size` according to the actual number of devices.

```bash
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"  # not needed on A2
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
vllm serve your_model_path \
    --served-model-name qwen3 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --max-num-seqs 100 \
    --max-model-len 40960 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --quantization ascend \
    --distributed_executor_backend "mp" \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --additional-config '{"weight_nz_mode": 2}' \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
    --port 8000 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "eagle3", "model": "your_eagle3_model_path", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
```

## Verification

After the service is started, send a chat completion request: replace `localhost:8000` with the actual server IP and `--port` value, and `model` must match `--served-model-name`.

```shell
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "qwen3",
        "messages": [
            {"role": "user", "content": "Give me a short introduction to large language models."}
        ],
        "temperature": 0.6,
        "top_p": 0.95,
        "top_k": 20,
        "max_completion_tokens": 4096
    }'
```

Expected result: HTTP 200, returning a JSON response containing the `choices` field (with the generated text).

## Prerequisites

### Model Weights

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | Download Links |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-27B (BF16 version) |  | ModelScope \ |
| Qwen3.5-27B-w8a8 (quantized version) |  | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.6-27B (BF16 version) | 1 Ascend 950DT series product (96GB × 8) node or 1 | ModelScope \ |
| Qwen3.6-27B-w8a8 (quantized version) |  | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.6-27B-w8a8-mxfp8 (quantized version) | 1 Ascend 950DT series product (96GB × 8) node | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.6-27B-w8a8c8-mxfp8 (quantized version) | 1 Ascend 950DT series product (96GB × 8) node | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.6-27B-w8a8-310p (quantized version) |  | ModelScope |

`Qwen3.6-27B-w8a8c8-mxfp8` (W8A8 MXFP8 quantization with C8 MXFP8 KV cache): starting the service with `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` is recommended for long-sequence scenarios.

It is recommended to download the model weights to a shared directory for multiple nodes, for example `/root/.cache/`.

**Path note**: download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record that directory. Make sure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches that directory.

### Verify multi-node communication

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to verify multi-node communication according to [Verify the multi-node communication environment](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

## Installation

Select an image based on your machine type and start the docker image on the node; refer to [Using docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image).

**We recommend using the `v0.30.0` version** of the `vllm-ascend` image to ensure the best compatibility and to get the latest features. As the minimum version requirement, use `vllm-ascend:v0.17.0rc1` (or higher) for `Qwen3.5-27B` and `vllm-ascend:v0.18.0rc1` (or higher) for `Qwen3.6-27B`.

Start the docker image on each node.

```shell
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a5
export NAME=vllm-ascend

docker run --rm \
    --name $NAME \
    --net=host \
    --shm-size=1g \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci1 \
    --device /dev/davinci2 \
    --device /dev/davinci3 \
    --device /dev/davinci4 \
    --device /dev/davinci5 \
    --device /dev/davinci6 \
    --device /dev/davinci7 \
    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    --device /dev/ummu \
    --device /dev/uburma \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /etc/hccl_rootinfo.json:/etc/hccl_rootinfo.json \
    -v /etc/hixlep/:/etc/hixlep/ \
    -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
    -v /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/sbin \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/sbin/npu-smi:/usr/local/sbin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/lib64:/usr/lib64 \
    -it $IMAGE bash
```

After docker starts successfully, you can verify the running container service by executing `docker ps`. The expected result is that the container `vllm-ascend` has the status `Up`, confirming that docker was installed successfully.

## Deployment

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment completes Prefill and Decode within the same node, suitable for development, testing, and medium-scale inference scenarios. The `Qwen3.6-27B`, `Qwen3.6-27B-w8a8-mxfp8`, and `Qwen3.6-27B-w8a8c8-mxfp8` models can all be deployed on 1 Ascend 950DT series product (96GB × 8). Quantized versions need to be started with the `--quantization ascend` parameter.

`Qwen3.5-27B` and `Qwen3.6-27B` share the same MTP head design, so the `qwen3_5_mtp` speculative decoding method can be used for both.

The following example applies to Ascend 950DT series products. Quantized versions require `--quantization ascend`.

[Qwen3.6-27B-w8a8c8-mxfp8](#__tabbed_5_1)

Start command:

```bash
#!/bin/sh
# Load model from ModelScope to speed up download
export MODEL_PATH=Eco-Tech/Qwen3.6-27B-w8a8c8-mxfp8
export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
sysctl kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download

vllm serve $MODEL_PATH \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --quantization ascend \
    --kv-cache-dtype mxfp8 \
    --served-model-name qwen3.6 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --max-model-len 153600 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --allowed-local-media-path / \
    --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 \
    --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
    --mm-processor-cache-type shm \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1,4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,36,40,44,48,52,56,60,64,68,72,76,80,84,88,92,96,100,104,108,112,116,120,124,128],"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding": true, "enable_flashcomm1": true}'
```

Key parameter descriptions:

- `--data-parallel-size 1` and `--tensor-parallel-size 1` are common settings for the data parallel (DP) and tensor parallel (TP) sizes.
- `--max-model-len` indicates the context length, i.e., the maximum value of input plus output for a single request. The Qwen3.6-27B model supports up to 262144.
- `--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of requests each DP group is allowed to process. If the number of requests sent to the service exceeds this limit, the excess requests stay in the waiting state and are not scheduled. Note that the time spent in the waiting state is also counted in metrics such as TTFT and TPOT. Therefore, when testing performance, it is usually recommended that `--max-num-seqs` * `--data-parallel-size` >= the actual total concurrency.
- `--max-num-batched-tokens` indicates the maximum number of tokens the model can process in a single step. Currently, vLLM v1 scheduling enables ChunkPrefill/SplitFuse by default, which means: (1) if the input length of a request is greater than `--max-num-batched-tokens`, it will be computed in multiple rounds according to `--max-num-batched-tokens` (2) Decode requests are scheduled first, and prefill requests are scheduled only when capacity is available. Usually, if `--max-num-batched-tokens` is set larger, the overall latency will be lower, but the pressure on HBM memory (activation usage) will be greater.
- `--gpu-memory-utilization` indicates the proportion of HBM that vLLM will use for actual inference. Its essential role is to compute the available kv_cache size. During the warm-up phase (called profile run in vLLM), vLLM records the peak HBM memory usage during one inference run with an input size of `--max-num-batched-tokens`. The available kv_cache size is then computed as: `--gpu-memory-utilization` * HBM size - peak HBM memory usage. Therefore, the larger the value of `--gpu-memory-utilization`, the more kv_cache can be used. However, since the HBM memory usage in the warm-up phase may differ from actual inference (for example, due to EP load imbalance), setting `--gpu-memory-utilization` too high may cause OOM (out of memory) problems during actual inference. The default value is `0.9`.
- Prefix caching is enabled by default, and the above example uses the default value. To disable it, add `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. For workloads with long shared prefixes, finer-grained hybrid prefix matching can be enabled via `--enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 16`. The matching unit must evenly divide the block size of each KV cache group. Smaller units can reuse more partial physical pages, at the cost of extra hash metadata, copy-on-write operations, and an extra prefill split at the final match boundary.
- `--quantization ascend` indicates that quantization is used. To disable quantization, remove this option.
- `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` enables C8 (MXFP8 KV cache) and is required for `Qwen3.6-27B-w8a8c8-mxfp8` weights. It stores the KV cache of full-attention layers as FP8 (E4M3) with E8M0 scaling factors, and runs full-attention layers on a dedicated QFA (quant flash attention) kernel. W8A8C8 weights bring performance improvements in long-sequence scenarios. When using this option, `--block-size` must be a multiple of `512` (if not set, it defaults to `512`).
- For short-sequence scenarios (for example, a 16K input length), it is recommended to use W8A8 weights instead (for example, `Qwen3.6-27B-w8a8-mxfp8`). When serving W8A8 weights, remove `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` from the start command. Note that C8 quantization is only supported on Ascend 950PR&950DT series products.
- `--speculative-config` uses `qwen3_5_mtp` for `Qwen3.6-27B`, because it shares the same MTP head design as `Qwen3.5-27B`.
- `--compilation-config` contains configurations related to the aclgraph graph mode. The most important configurations are `"cudagraph_mode"` and `"cudagraph_capture_sizes"`, whose meanings are as follows: `"cudagraph_mode"`: indicates the specific graph mode. Currently `"PIECEWISE"` and `"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"` are supported. Graph mode is mainly used to reduce operator scheduling overhead. Currently `"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"` is recommended. `"cudagraph_capture_sizes"`: specifies the batch size tiers for captured graphs. The default value is `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40,..., --max-num-seqs]`. In graph mode, the batch size of each captured graph is fixed, and an actual batch size between two adjacent capture sizes is automatically padded up to the next capture size. Currently the default setting is recommended. This value only needs to be set separately in certain scenarios to achieve optimal performance.
- `--allowed-local-media-path` allows the API server to read local images or videos from the specified directory when processing multimodal inputs. In this example, `/` whitelists the entire file system. This is security-sensitive and should be enabled only in trusted environments.
- `--mm-processor-cache-gb` sets the size of the multimodal processor cache (in GiB), used to avoid repeatedly processing past multimodal inputs. This cache is duplicated in each API server process and engine core process, so the total host memory usage is the cache size multiplied by the number of these processes. A value of `0` completely disables this cache.
- `--mm-encoder-tp-mode` indicates how to optimize multimodal encoder inference using tensor parallelism (TP). `data` splits the batched encoder input data across TP ranks while each rank holds the full encoder weights, and is recommended when there are multimodal inputs. The default mode `weights` splits the encoder weights across TP ranks.
- `--mm-processor-cache-type` sets the cache type used by the multimodal preprocessor and mapper. `shm` uses a shared-memory FIFO cache, while the default `lru` uses a mirrored LRU cache.
- `--additional-config` contains Ascend-specific optimization options: `"enable_cpu_binding": true` enables native Ascend CPU binding, binding worker processes, key runtime threads, memory pages, and NPU interrupts to CPU ranges close to the driven NPU, reducing cross-NUMA traffic and thread preemption and improving latency stability. It is enabled by default starting from vllm-ascend v0.18.0rc1. `"enable_flashcomm1": true` enables the FlashComm communication optimization, splitting the tensor-parallel AllReduce into Reduce-Scatter and All-Gather to reduce communication overhead and improve prefill throughput.

Common issues tip: if you encounter problems, refer to [Common FAQs](../../faqs.html) for troubleshooting.

Service verification:

If the service starts successfully, the following startup logs will be displayed:

```text
(APIServer pid=<pid>) INFO:     Started server process [<pid>]
(APIServer pid=<pid>) INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
(APIServer pid=<pid>) INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

For functional tests (for example, `completions` and `chat.completions` curl examples with expected responses), refer to [Section 6](#6-functional-verification).

## Verification

After the service starts, you can invoke the model by sending prompts. Two API interfaces are supported: `completions` and `chat.completions`. Use the `--served-model-name` you configured (`qwen3.5` for `Qwen3.5-27B` and `qwen3.6` for `Qwen3.6-27B`).

**Completions API：**

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "qwen3.5",
        "prompt": "The future of AI is",
        "max_tokens": 50,
        "temperature": 0
    }'
```

**Note**: for `Qwen3.6-27B`, set `"model": "qwen3.6"` in the request body.

**Chat Completions API：**

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "qwen3.5",
        "messages": [
            {"role": "user", "content": "The future of AI is"}
        ],
        "max_completion_tokens": 1024,
        "temperature": 0.7,
        "top_p": 0.95
    }'
```

**Note**: for `Qwen3.6-27B`, set `"model": "qwen3.6"` in the request body.

Expected result: the service returns HTTP 200 OK. The JSON response contains a `choices` field and the generated text. The following is an example output of the completions API (content is truncated to keep it concise):

```json
{
    "id": "cmpl-xxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "object": "text_completion",
    "created": 1780971952,
    "model": "qwen3.5",
    "choices": [
        {
            "index": 0,
            "text": "The future of AI is a rapidly evolving landscape with breakthroughs in natural language understanding, multimodal reasoning, and autonomous agents. As models grow more capable and efficient...",
            "logprobs": null,
            "finish_reason": "length"
        }
    ],
    "usage": {
        "prompt_tokens": 4,
        "total_tokens": 54,
        "completion_tokens": 50
    }
}
```

## Prerequisites

### Model Weights

| Weight version | Hardware requirement | KV cache selection | Download link |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (BF16 version) | 2 Ascend 950DT series product (96 GB x 8) nodes | The baseline uses auto | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mtp (quantized version) |  | Follows the checkpoint KV quantization scheme | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a8-mtp (quantized version) |  | Follows the checkpoint KV quantization scheme | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mxfp8 (quantized version) | 1 Ascend 950DT series product (96 GB x 8) node | Check the KV metadata; the model name alone is not enough to determine it | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a4-mxfp4 (quantized version) | 1 Ascend 950DT series product (96 GB x 8) node | Check the KV metadata; the model name alone is not enough to determine it | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8c8-mxfp8 (quantized version) | 1 Ascend 950DT series product (96 GB x 8) node | Supported C8 schemes use mxfp8 | ModelScope |

Note

`--quantization ascend` selects the Ascend model quantization implementation`--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` selects MXFP8 KV cache storage. The two configure different parts of inference. Enable `mxfp8` only when the checkpoint is supported and has the required KV scale metadata. W4A8/W8A8 names or the MXFP weight format itself do not establish C8 KV cache compatibility. Do not copy the KV settings of W4A8C8 or W8A8C8 to other checkpoints before checking the quantization notes and service logs. Make sure the weight version, tokenizer, quantization metadata, and KV cache settings on P and D are consistent.

It is recommended to download the model weights to a directory shared across multiple nodes, for example `/root/.cache/`, so that all service nodes can load the same path.

**Path note**: download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record that directory. Make sure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches that directory.

### Verify multi-node communication

For multi-node deployment, verify inter-node connectivity according to the instructions in [Verify multi-node communication](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

Use service IPs that can reach each other on all nodes. In the following scripts, `local_ip` must belong to `nic_name`.

For PD deployment of Ascend 950DT series products, prepare the [Mooncake communication environment](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html) and mount the required host-specific communication resources into each service container. When setting `ascend_local_comm_res_path=/etc/hixlep`, make sure `/etc/hixlep` contains the configuration required for that host.

## Installation

Select an appropriate image for your hardware and start the container on each node. For details, refer to [Using Docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image).

For PD deployment, use the same vLLM-Ascend release image and dependency versions on P and D.

Before starting the container, run the following commands as root on the **host machine**. Do not run these commands inside the inference service container: the container mounts `/sys` and `/proc/sys` read-only, so writes to the CPU governor will fail and `sysctl` will be silently ignored (still returning 0), making tuning appear successful while it actually does not take effect.

```bash
# Host CPU governor and kernel tuning (run on the host, not in the container).
echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
sysctl kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
```

Start a Docker container on each node.

```bash
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a5
export NAME=vllm-ascend

docker run --rm \
  --name $NAME \
  --net=host \
  --shm-size=64g \
  --ulimit memlock=-1 \
  --device /dev/davinci0 \
  --device /dev/davinci1 \
  --device /dev/davinci2 \
  --device /dev/davinci3 \
  --device /dev/davinci4 \
  --device /dev/davinci5 \
  --device /dev/davinci6 \
  --device /dev/davinci7 \
  --device /dev/davinci_manager \
  --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
  --device /dev/ummu \
  --device /dev/uburma \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver \
  -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
  -v /etc/hccl_rootinfo.json:/etc/hccl_rootinfo.json \
  -v /etc/hixlep/:/etc/hixlep/ \
  -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
  -v /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/sbin \
  -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
  -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
  -v /usr/local/sbin/npu-smi:/usr/local/sbin/npu-smi \
  -itd $IMAGE bash
```

Keep the `/usr/lib64` that comes with the container in the selected image. Mounting an entire host directory over this path may shadow the system libraries provided by the image and break the matched CANN/runtime dependencies; even if such a whole-directory mount is set to read-only, it cannot prevent libraries from being shadowed. If the selected URMA/RoCE transport requires additional host libraries, mount only the specific compatible files or vendor directories required by its installation guide, read-only, and verify the library load paths inside the container.

Note

For the 397B long-context deployment scheme given in this document, `--shm-size=64g` is recommended. Configure both sufficient shared memory and an unlimited memlock setting: a 1g shared memory or the default 64 MB locked memory limit is too small, causing worker startup and memory profiling to fail with `torch.OutOfMemoryError` / `aclrtMallocHostWithCfg error 207001` (host memory allocation failure), and HCCL link establishment may time out. If the container runtime does not allow `--ulimit memlock=-1`, configure the host/runtime policy or grant the required minimum capability. Increasing only `--shm-size` does not lift the memlock limit.

The CPU governor and `sysctl` tuning commands must be run on the host machine before starting the container; see the host preparation code block at the top of this section. Do not run these commands inside the inference service container, because `/sys` and `/proc/sys` in the container are read-only.

After entering the actual service container on each node, check the executable, version, and import paths:

```shell
command -v python3 vllm
python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.metadata as metadata
import sys

import torch_npu
import vllm
import vllm_ascend

print("Python:", sys.executable)
for module in (vllm, vllm_ascend, torch_npu):
    print(module.__name__, module.__file__)
for package in (
    "vllm", "vllm-ascend", "torch", "torch-npu", "triton-ascend",
    "mooncake-transfer-engine-npu", "mooncake-transfer-engine",
):
    try:
        print(package, metadata.version(package))
    except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
        print(package, "not installed under this distribution name")
PY
```

If you want to deploy a multi-node service, set up the same environment on each node.

## Deployment

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment runs Prefill and Decode on the same node at the same time. It is suitable for functional verification and long-context serving.

Run the following script on a single Ascend 950DT series product node (96 GB x 8) for online inference. The quantized versions (`Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mxfp8` and `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a4-mxfp4`) can be deployed on a single node and require `--quantization ascend`.

```shell
#!/bin/sh

# Load model from ModelScope to speed up download.
export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=400
export HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE=0
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"
export VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_PREFETCH_MLP=1
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
MODEL_PATH="Eco-Tech/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a4-mxfp4"
vllm serve "${MODEL_PATH}" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --served-model-name qwen3.5 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-model-len 133000 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --async-scheduling \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding": true, "enable_fused_mc2": 1, "enable_flashcomm1": true}'
```

Common issues tip: if the service fails to start, HBM is insufficient, or requests are not scheduled as expected, refer first to the [Common FAQ](../../faqs.html), then see the model-specific FAQ in [Section 10](#10-faq).

**Key parameters:**

`--data-parallel-size 1` uses one DP group. `--tensor-parallel-size` is 16 in the A3 example and 8 in the 950DT example.

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--max-model-len` is the maximum input plus output length of a single request. Increase this value only when the KV cache is sufficient.

`--max-num-seqs` is the maximum number of active requests scheduled per DP group. When performing performance tests, set `--max-num-seqs * --data-parallel-size` to be greater than or equal to the test concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in a single scheduling step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--gpu-memory-utilization` controls the proportion of HBM that vLLM can use to compute the KV cache capacity. A higher value increases the KV cache size, but may trigger OOM if the runtime memory is higher than that of the profile run.

`--enable-prefix-caching` enables prefix caching. For Qwen3.5, when the hybrid KV cache manager adjusts the block size to a larger value, short prefixes may not be cached.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the quantized weights above. Remove this option when deploying a BF16 model.

`--speculative-config` enables Qwen3.5 MTP speculative decoding. If the workload is sensitive to first-token latency, or MTP is unstable in your environment, reduce `num_speculative_tokens` or remove this option.

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full decode ACLGraph replay to reduce scheduling overhead.

`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` selects Model Runner V1 for the single-node example above.

`--additional-config` configures Ascend-specific optimizations: `enable_cpu_binding=true` enables native Ascend CPU binding`enable_fused_mc2=1` selects dispatch-FFN-combine, which the single-node 950DT and A3 examples use to be compatible with the MTP and batching configurations described in the document`2` selects CANN MegaMoe, which should be enabled only when the CANN/operator stack matches and the token shape restrictions are supported`0` disables the fused path. `enable_flashcomm1=true` enables MoE sequence parallelism across TP ranks and requires `--enable-expert-parallel` and a TP size greater than 1.

### Request forwarding

Use the proxy that matches the actual connector, rather than selecting a proxy based on the hardware name. The standard proxy scripts are located in `examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/`run the commands from that directory. Replace the example hosts with reachable service IPs and use the HTTP port of each service. P, D, and the client must use the same `--served-model-name`.

| Connector | Request order | Proxy | Applicable scope |
|---|---|---|---|

Equal TP sizes do not mean that these connectors are interchangeable. For non-equal TP, verify the direction, divisibility, replicated KV heads, hybrid state layout, and quantization support of the selected implementation. The TP8 to TP4 example does not imply support for arbitrary TP ratios or the reverse direction. Use scripts from the same vLLM-Ascend revision as the service stack.

Use the complete proxy command corresponding to the selected deployment:

[950DT two-machine 1P1D](#553-proxy): P and D use their respective high-speed service IP; the D backend uses HTTP port `30050`.

Do not use the DP RPC port or the Mooncake KV transfer port as the proxy backend. If requests reach the proxy but no output is returned, verify the `/health` endpoints of P and D from the proxy host, confirm that the configured backend addresses exactly match the `--host` and HTTP port of each service, and then run the end-to-end check in [Section 6](#6-functional-verification).

## Verification

Wait for both P and D to report ready, verify each HTTP service, and then start the matching proxy. For single-node and MP deployments, use the API endpoint on node 0. For PD disaggregation, send generation requests through the proxy so that the test covers KV transfer.

```shell
curl -f "http://<prefill_ip>:<prefill_http_port>/health"
curl -f "http://<decode_ip>:<decode_http_port>/health"
curl -f "http://<proxy_ip>:<proxy_port>/healthcheck"
curl -f "http://<prefill_ip>:<prefill_http_port>/v1/models"
```

Check that the advertised model name matches the request. A health check only confirms HTTP readiness and does not verify the PD data path. Send several short requests first, then send concurrent requests that can complete and reuse cache slots, and check the P, D, and proxy logs.

```shell
curl "http://<server_ip>:<port>/v1/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.5",
    "prompt": "The future of AI is",
    "max_tokens": 50,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

Expected result: the HTTP status code is 200, and `choices` in the JSON response contains non-empty, coherent generated text. Also verify a chat request once using the chat template of this checkpoint; sending only a short completion request is not sufficient as an accuracy test. Before running the full benchmark, check for transfer errors, empty results, repeated punctuation, and abnormal repetition. Repeat the test with non-streaming requests first and then with streaming requests to verify the proxy's chunked response path.

### Function calling

To enable tool calling, append the following options to the `vllm serve` command. For PD deployment, add them to both the Prefill and Decode commands and restart both services.

```text
--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

`--enable-auto-tool-choice` allows the model to choose tools, `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` parses tool calls, and `--reasoning-parser qwen3` separates the reasoning process from the final answer.

Send a chat request containing a tool definition to the service endpoint. For PD deployment, use the proxy endpoint.

```shell
curl "http://<server_ip>:<port>/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.5",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Use get_weather to check the current weather in Beijing."}
    ],
    "tools": [{
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get the current weather for a city.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["city"]
        }
      }
    }],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "max_tokens": 2048,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

When the model selects this tool, check whether `choices[0].message.tool_calls` contains the function name `get_weather` and a JSON argument string that sets `city` to `Beijing`. The client must execute the function and then send the assistant's tool call message together with a `role: "tool"` result message with a matching `tool_call_id` in the next request to obtain the final answer. The service process only parses tool calls and does not execute the function.

## Prerequisites

### Model Weights

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | Download Links |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (BF16 version) | 1 Ascend 950DT series product (96GB x 8) node | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8 (quantized version) |  | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8-mxfp8 (quantized version) | 1 Ascend 950DT series product (96GB x 8) node | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8c8-mxfp8 (quantized version) | 1 Ascend 950DT series product (96GB x 8) node | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w4a8-mxfp (quantized version) | 1 Ascend 950DT series product (96GB x 8) node | ModelScope |

It is recommended to download the model weights to a directory shared across multiple nodes, for example `/root/.cache/`.

**Path note**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record the path. Make sure that the model path in the subsequent deployment commands matches this directory.

## Installation

For the complete installation guide, refer to [Using docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image).

```bash
# Download the model weight to /root/.cache in advance.
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a5
export NAME=vllm-ascend

docker run --rm \
  --name $NAME \
  --net=host \
  --shm-size=500g \
  --device /dev/davinci_manager \
  --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
  --device /dev/ummu \
  --device /dev/uburma \
  --device /dev/davinci0 \
  --device /dev/davinci1 \
  --device /dev/davinci2 \
  --device /dev/davinci3 \
  --device /dev/davinci4 \
  --device /dev/davinci5 \
  --device /dev/davinci6 \
  --device /dev/davinci7 \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/firmware:/usr/local/Ascend/firmware \
  -v /root/host:/root/host  \
  -v /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/sbin \
  -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
  -v /var/log/npu:/usr/slog \
  -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
  -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
```
