After entering the container, verify that vLLM and vLLM-Ascend can be imported:

```shell
python -c "import vllm, vllm_ascend; print('vllm and vllm_ascend are ready')"
```

## Deployment

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment runs Prefill and Decode on the same node at the same time. `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8-mxfp8` can be deployed on a single NPU of an Ascend 950DT series product (96GB x 8) node. Quantized versions require `--quantization ascend`.

Run the following script to perform online inference with `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8-mxfp8` on a single NPU of an Ascend 950DT series product (96GB x 8) node, with a maximum context length of 135168.

```shell
export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3000
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export OMP_PROC_BIND=false
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1

vllm serve Eco-Tech/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8-mxfp8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.6 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --quantization ascend \
  --safetensors-load-strategy lazy \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 135168 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":true,"ascend_compilation_config":{"enable_npugraph_ex":true,"enable_static_kernel":true,"enable_super_kernel":false}}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching
```

Note

When using C8 weights (`Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8c8-mxfp8`), add the following options to the `vllm serve` deployment command:

```shell
--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8
```

Enabling static kernel generation increases compile time during startup. Wait for the service to finish graph capture and report ready before sending requests.

**Key parameters:**

- `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`, `--tensor-parallel-size 1`, and `--data-parallel-size 1` run a single model instance on the selected NPU, without tensor parallelism or data parallelism. Adjust the visible devices according to the available NPUs.
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` selects Model Runner V2 for this deployment example.
- `--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the W8A8 MXFP8 model.
- `--safetensors-load-strategy lazy` uses lazy loading for Safetensors model weights.
- `--max-model-len 135168` sets the maximum input plus output length of a single request. Make sure enough KV cache is provided for the required context length.
- `--max-num-seqs 128` sets the maximum number of active requests scheduled concurrently. If KV cache or graph capture memory is insufficient, decrease this value.
- `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096` limits the number of tokens processed in a single scheduling step. Increase this value only after checking prefill throughput and activation memory usage.
- `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90` sets the proportion of device memory available to the model executor when computing the KV cache capacity. If startup or runtime requests report OOM, decrease this value.
- `--speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'` enables Qwen3.5-style MTP speculative decoding, using three draft tokens per step. Adjust the number of speculative tokens according to the acceptance rate, request concurrency, and measured latency and throughput.
- `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full decode ACLGraph replay to reduce scheduling overhead.
- `--additional-config` enables native Ascend CPU binding via `enable_cpu_binding`. Its `ascend_compilation_config` enables npugraph_ex and static kernel generation`enable_super_kernel:false` keeps Super Kernel disabled instead of inheriting the static kernel setting.
- `--enable-prefix-caching` enables cached KV block reuse for requests with shared prefixes. For long-context workloads, monitor the KV cache usage.
- For the C8 weight version, `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` selects MXFP8 KV cache storage.

Common issues tip: if the service fails to start, HBM is insufficient, or requests are not scheduled as expected, refer first to the [Common FAQ](../../faqs.html), then see the FAQ for this model in [Section 10](#10-faq).

**Service verification:**

Loading model weights and capturing computation graphs may take some time, especially when static kernel generation is enabled in the 950DT example. Startup duration depends on storage speed and the selected configuration. Use the health check below to confirm that the service is ready.

Use the API port configured in the selected deployment command. For example, check via port `8000` on the service node or container of the 950DT deployment:

```shell
curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
```

For other deployments, use their configured API port. A healthy service returns HTTP `200`. If the check fails, look for errors in the startup logs and wait for initialization to complete. After the health check passes, use [Section 6](#6-functional-verification) to verify that the model can generate responses.

## Verification

After the server starts, send requests to verify the basic functionality of the model.

```shell
curl http://<server_ip>:<port>/v1/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.6",
    "prompt": "The future of AI is",
    "max_tokens": 50,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

Expected result: the HTTP status code is 200, and the JSON response contains the `choices` field with the generated text.

## Prerequisites

- Hardware: 1 A3 series (64GB x 16) node, running Prefill and Decode on the same node.
- Weights: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` (BF16 version), downloaded from ModelScope.
- Quantization: this record uses BF16 weights; do not add `--quantization ascend` during deployment.
- Path: it is recommended to download the model weights to a directory shared across multiple nodes, for example `/root/.cache/`, and record that path for use in the deployment command.

## Installation

Start the A3 series Docker container: the image is `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a3`, the container name is `vllm-ascend`, mapping devices davinci0 to davinci15 and the driver path.

```bash
# Download the model weight to /root/.cache in advance.
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a3
export NAME=vllm-ascend

docker run --rm \
  --name $NAME \
  --net=host \
  --shm-size=1g \
  --device /dev/davinci0 \
  --device /dev/davinci1 \
  --device /dev/davinci2 \
  --device /dev/davinci3 \
  --device /dev/davinci4 \
  --device /dev/davinci5 \
  --device /dev/davinci6 \
  --device /dev/davinci7 \
  --device /dev/davinci8 \
  --device /dev/davinci9 \
  --device /dev/davinci10 \
  --device /dev/davinci11 \
  --device /dev/davinci12 \
  --device /dev/davinci13 \
  --device /dev/davinci14 \
  --device /dev/davinci15 \
  --device /dev/davinci_manager \
  --device /dev/devmm_svm \
  --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
  -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool \
  -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
  -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
  -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
  -it $IMAGE bash
```

After entering the container, verify that `vllm` and `vllm_ascend` can be imported.

```shell
python -c "import vllm, vllm_ascend; print('vllm and vllm_ascend are ready')"
```

## Deployment

Start the single-node online service: replace the model path with the recorded BF16 weight directory and remove `--quantization ascend`; `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1` and `--tensor-parallel-size 2` correspond to two cards, adjust according to the available devices.

```shell
# Load model from ModelScope to speed up download.
export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3000
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export OMP_PROC_BIND=false
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
vllm serve Eco-Tech/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --quantization ascend \
  --served-model-name qwen3.6 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-model-len 135168 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --safetensors-load-strategy lazy \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --dtype float16 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":true, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true}'
```

## Verification

Replace `<server_ip>` with the service node IP and `<port>` with the `8000` used in the deployment command; keep the model name in the request body consistent with `--served-model-name`.

```shell
curl http://<server_ip>:<port>/v1/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.6",
    "prompt": "The future of AI is",
    "max_tokens": 50,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

Expected result: the HTTP status code is 200, and the JSON response contains the `choices` field with the generated text.

> Source: https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/zh-cn/v0.30.0/tutorials/models/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.html (v0.30.0, A2 series / A3 series tab)

## Prerequisites

- Hardware: 1 Atlas 300I DUO node; Prefill and Decode are completed within the same single node, requiring at least 2 devices.
- Weights: `Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-310p` (quantized version), downloaded from ModelScope.
- Quantization: the quantized version needs to be started with the `--quantization ascend` parameter.
- Path: replace `MODEL_PATH` with the ModelScope model ID or a local weight directory path.
- Restriction: currently only tensor parallelism scenarios are supported; choose TP=2 or TP=4 according to the available devices.

## Installation

Start the Docker container: the image is `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-310p`, the container name is `vllm-ascend`, mapping devices davinci0 to davinci7 and the driver path.

```bash
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-310p
export NAME=vllm-ascend

docker run --rm \
    --name $NAME \
    --shm-size=1g \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci1 \
    --device /dev/davinci2 \
    --device /dev/davinci3 \
    --device /dev/davinci4 \
    --device /dev/davinci5 \
    --device /dev/davinci6 \
    --device /dev/davinci7 \
    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/devmm_svm \
    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
    -it $IMAGE bash
```

After entering the container, verify that vLLM and vLLM-Ascend can be imported.

```shell
python -c "import vllm, vllm_ascend; print('vllm and vllm_ascend are ready')"
```

Expected result: `vllm and vllm_ascend are ready` is output.

## Deployment

Start the single-node online service: replace `MODEL_PATH` with `Eco-Tech/Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-310p` or a local weight directory, and set `--tensor-parallel-size` to 2 or 4 according to the available devices.

```bash
#!/bin/sh
# Load model from ModelScope to speed up download
export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True

# Model weight path; can be a ModelScope model id (e.g., Eco-Tech/Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8) or a local directory path
# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
export MODEL_PATH=Eco-Tech/Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-310p

vllm serve $MODEL_PATH \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --port 8000 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --served-model-name qwen3.8 \
    --max-num-seqs 128 \
    --max-model-len 16384 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 \
    --dtype float16 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [2,16]}' \
    --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config": {"enable_npugraph_ex": false}}'
```

## Verification

Send requests on the service node; `127.0.0.1:8000` corresponds to the `--host` and `--port` configured in the deployment command, and keep the model name in the request body consistent with `--served-model-name`.

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "qwen3.8",
        "prompt": "The future of AI is",
        "max_tokens": 50,
        "temperature": 0.7
    }'
```

Expected result: the service returns HTTP 200 OK. The JSON response contains a `choices` field with generated text.

> Source: https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/zh-cn/v0.30.0/tutorials/models/Qwen3.8-27B.html (v0.30.0, Atlas 300I DUO tab)

## Prerequisites

- Hardware: 1 Atlas 800I A3 (64GB × 8) node; Prefill and Decode are completed within a single node.
- Weights: `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8-mtp` (quantized version), requiring 1 Atlas 800 A3 (64GB × 8) node for serving.
- Quantization: the start command loads the Ascend-compatible W8A8 checkpoint via `--quantization ascend`.
- Path: replace `MODEL_PATH` with the directory recorded when downloading the model weights, and mount that directory to `/models` in the container.
- Check: before changing the context length, concurrency, or memory utilization, re-verify the memory capacity with `npu-smi info`.

## Installation

Start the Docker container on each A3 node: the image is `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:qwen3.8-next-a3`; replace `/path/to/models` in `-v /path/to/models:/models` with the host weight directory.

```bash
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:qwen3.8-next-a3
export NAME=vllm-ascend-qwen38-flash-next

docker pull "$IMAGE"

docker run --rm \
    --name "$NAME" \
    --shm-size=16g \
    --net=host \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci1 \
    --device /dev/davinci2 \
    --device /dev/davinci3 \
    --device /dev/davinci4 \
    --device /dev/davinci5 \
    --device /dev/davinci6 \
    --device /dev/davinci7 \
    --device /dev/davinci8 \
    --device /dev/davinci9 \
    --device /dev/davinci10 \
    --device /dev/davinci11 \
    --device /dev/davinci12 \
    --device /dev/davinci13 \
    --device /dev/davinci14 \
    --device /dev/davinci15 \
    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/devmm_svm \
    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64 \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /path/to/models:/models \
    -it "$IMAGE" bash
```

After entering the container, verify that vLLM and vLLM-Ascend can be imported normally.

```shell
python -c "import vllm, vllm_ascend; print('vllm and vllm-ascend are ready')"
```

## Deployment

Start the single-node online service inside the container: `MODEL_PATH=/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8-mtp` corresponds to the `/models` mount directory of the container; the service listens on port `8088`, adjust according to the actual environment.

```bash
unset CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH CPATH C_INCLUDE_PATH
source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

export MODEL_PATH=/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8-mtp
export VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_QSA_LIGHTNING_INDEXER=1
export VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_QSA_E3V=1
unset VLLM_ASCEND_FORCE_QSA_REFERENCE

vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8088 \
    --served-model-name qwen3.8-flash-next \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --quantization ascend \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
    --data-parallel-start-rank 0 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --max-model-len 131072 \
    --max-num-seqs 8 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --mamba-cache-mode align \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32],"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"enforce_eager":true}' \
    --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":true,"ascend_compilation_config":{"fuse_norm_quant":false}}'
```

## Verification

Send requests to `127.0.0.1:8088` configured in the deployment command, and keep the model name in the request body consistent with `--served-model-name`.

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "qwen3.8-flash-next",
        "messages": [
            {"role": "user", "content": "Who are you?"}
        ],
        "max_tokens": 1024,
        "temperature": 0
    }'
```

Expected result: the service returns HTTP 200 OK.

> Source: https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/zh-cn/v0.30.0/tutorials/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.html (v0.30.0, A3 series products tab)

guideMd:
## Prerequisites

- Hardware: 1 Atlas 800I A2 inference server; the feature matrix supports world sizes 1, 2, 4, and 8.
- Weights: download floating-point weights from the deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B repository on Hugging Face.
- Quantization: W8A8 quantized weights need to be generated with the msModelSlim tool; note that this quantization method is only supported on Atlas 800I A2 servers.
- Environment: the host machine must have the NPU driver and firmware installed, and the Docker version must be 24.x.x or higher.
- Path: `weight_path` indicates the model weight path; fill in `modelWeightPath` in the configuration file with that path.

## Installation

Install the NPU driver and firmware: replace `<chip_type>` with the product series, `<version>` with the corresponding version, and `<arch>` with the system architecture, and select the community or commercial version of the corresponding version according to the product series and model.

```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run --full --force
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run --full
```

Generate W8A8 quantized weights: replace `{floating-point weight path}` and `{W8A8 quantized weight path}` with actual directories; this quantization method is only supported on Atlas 800I A2 servers.

```shell
# Set CANN package environment variables
source /usr/local/Ascend/cann/set_env.sh
# Disable virtual memory
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:False
# Enter the atb-models directory
cd ${ATB_SPEED_HOME_PATH}
# Quantize DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, with fallback layers, antioutlier configured with the m1 algorithm, using the min-max quantization method, with a calibration dataset of 50 BoolQ samples, running computation on the NPU
bash examples/models/llama3/generate_quant_weight.sh -src {floating-point weight path} -dst {W8A8 quantized weight path} -type llama3.1_8b_w8a8
```

Start the container: replace `<container-name>` with the container name and `{IMAGE_ID}` with the obtained MindIE image ID.

```bash
docker run -it -d --net=host --shm-size=500g \
--name <container-name> \
-w /home \
--device=/dev/davinci0:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci1:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci2:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci3:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci_manager:rwm \
--device=/dev/hisi_hdc:rwm \
--device=/dev/devmm_svm:rwm \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver:ro \
-v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi:ro \
-v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi:ro \
-v /usr/local/sbin/:/usr/local/sbin:ro \
-v /home/weight:/home/weight:ro \
{IMAGE_ID} bash
```

## Deployment

Open the MindIE Service configuration file.

```shell
vim /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/latest/mindie-service/conf/config.json
```

Modify the configuration file: fill in `port`, `managementPort`, and `metricsPort` with custom ports, fill in `npuDeviceIds` with the available NPU IDs, replace `modelWeightPath` with the weight directory pointed to by `weight_path`, and set `worldSize` to one of 1, 2, 4, or 8 supported by the feature matrix.

```json
{
...
"ServerConfig" :
{
...
"port" : 1025, # Custom
"managementPort" : 1026, # Custom
"metricsPort" : 1027, # Custom
...
"httpsEnabled" : false,
...
},

"BackendConfig": {
...
```

guideMd:
## Prerequisites

- Hardware: inference with W8A8 quantized weights requires at least 2 Atlas 800I A2 (8*64G) servers.
- Weights: you can download the Ascend natively quantized W8A8 weights directly from the DeepSeek-V3-0324-w8a8 repository on Modelers, or generate them yourself according to the quantization instructions.
- Image: mindie:2.0.T3 or later is required; you need to apply for image permission in the Ascend community before downloading.
- Multi-machine: `rank_table_file.json` needs to be configured; the configuration on all machines must be consistent, and only `MIES_CONTAINER_IP` is the local machine IP address.
- Path: `{/path-to-weights}` indicates the model weight directory, and `{rank_table_file.json path}` indicates the path of this file on the host machine.

## Installation

Install the NPU driver and firmware: replace `<chip_type>` with the product series, `<version>` with the corresponding version, and `<arch>` with the system architecture, and select the community or commercial version of the corresponding version according to the product series and model.

```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run --full --force
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run --full
```

Start the container: replace `<container-name>` with the container name and `{IMAGE_ID}` with the obtained MindIE image ID, and mount the weight directory and rank_table_file.json on the host machine into the container.

```bash
docker run -it -d --net=host --shm-size=500g \
--name <container-name> \
-w /home \
--device=/dev/davinci0:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci1:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci2:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci3:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci_manager:rwm \
--device=/dev/hisi_hdc:rwm \
--device=/dev/devmm_svm:rwm \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver:ro \
-v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi:ro \
-v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi:ro \
-v /usr/local/sbin/:/usr/local/sbin:ro \
-v /home/weight:/home/weight:ro \
{IMAGE_ID} bash
```

## Deployment

Configure the memory pool extension segment feature.

```bash
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
```

Configure the service environment variables: replace `{container ip address}` with the local container IP and `{rank_table_file.json path}` with the path of that file; fill in only the local address for MIES_CONTAINER_IP on each machine.

```bash
export MIES_CONTAINER_IP={container ip address}
export RANKTABLEFILE={rank_table_file.json path}
```

Open the service configuration file.

```bash
cd /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/latest/mindie-service/
vim conf/config.json
```

Modify the service parameters: set `multiNodesInferEnabled` to true to enable multi-machine inference, fill in `npudeviceIds` with the available NPU IDs on the local machine, replace `modelWeightPath` with the weight path, and fill in `worldSize` with the number of cards actually participating in inference.

```json
"httpsEnabled" : false, # If the network environment is insecure, HTTPS communication is not enabled; that is, when "httpsEnabled"="false", there is a relatively high network security risk
...
"multiNodesInferEnabled" : true, # Enable multi-machine inference
...
# If security authentication is not required, set the following two parameters to false
"interCommTLSEnabled" : false,
"interNodeTLSEnabled" : false,
...
"npudeviceIds" : [[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]],
...
"modelName" : "DeepSeek-V3" # Does not affect service startup
        "modelWeightPath" : "weight path",
"worldSize":8,
```

The complete configuration example is for reference only; change `ipAddress` and `managementIpAddress` to the master node IP, and adjust the ports, weight path, and parallelism parameters according to the actual situation.

```json

        "httpsEnabled" : false,
        "fullTextEnabled" : false,
        "tlsCaPath" : "security/ca/",
        "tlsCaFile" : ["ca.pem"],
        "tlsCert" : "security/certs/server.pem",
        "tlsPk" : "security/keys/server.key.pem",
        "tlsCrlPath" : "security/certs/",
        "tlsCrlFiles" : ["server_crl.pem"],
        "managementTlsCaFile" : ["management_ca.pem"],
        "managementTlsCert" : "security/certs/management/server.pem",
        "managementTlsPk" : "security/keys/management/server.key.pem",
        "managementTlsCrlPath" : "security/management/certs/",
        "managementTlsCrlFiles" : ["server_crl.pem"],
        "metricsTlsCaFile" : ["metrics_ca.pem"],
        "metricsTlsCert" : "security/certs/metrics/server.pem",
        "metricsTlsPk" : "security/keys/metrics/server.key.pem",
        "metricsTlsCrlPath" : "security/metrics/certs/",
        "metricsTlsCrlFiles" : ["server_crl.pem"],
        "inferMode" : "standard",
        "interCommTLSEnabled" : false,
        "interCommPort" : 1121,
        "interCommTlsCaPath" : "security/grpc/ca/",
```

## Prerequisites

- Hardware: at least 2 Atlas 800I A2 (8*64G) inference servers; W8A8 quantized weight inference needs to be prepared according to this specification.
- Weights: you can download the original FP8 weights and then convert them, or download the Ascend natively quantized W8A8 weights from Modelers.
- Quantization: W8A8 mixed quantized weights are generated using the histogram quantization method; both MLA and MOE use W8A8 quantization.
- Environment: the host machine has the NPU driver and firmware installed, the Docker version is 24.x.x or higher, and the image uses mindie:2.0.T3 or later.
- Multi-machine: the service configuration on all machines must be consistent; only MIES_CONTAINER_IP is the local machine IP, and rank_table_file.json needs to be configured.

## Installation

Install the NPU driver and firmware: replace `<chip_type>` with the product series, `<version>` with the corresponding version, and `<arch>` with the system architecture, and select the community or commercial version of the corresponding version according to the product series and model.

```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run --full --force
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run --full
```

Set the group and permissions of the weight directory: replace `{/path-to-weights/DeepSeek-R1}` with the actual weight directory.

```sh
chown -R 1001:1001 {/path-to-weights/DeepSeek-R1}
chmod -R 750 {/path-to-weights/DeepSeek-R1}
```

Start the container: replace `<container-name>` with the container name, replace `{IMAGE_ID}` with the image ID (run `docker images` to view it), and modify the weight mount path according to the actual directory.

```bash
docker run -it -d --net=host --shm-size=500g \
--name <container-name> \
-w /home \
--device=/dev/davinci0:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci1:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci2:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci3:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci_manager:rwm \
--device=/dev/hisi_hdc:rwm \
--device=/dev/devmm_svm:rwm \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver:ro \
-v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi:ro \
-v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi:ro \
-v /usr/local/sbin/:/usr/local/sbin:ro \
-v /home/weight:/home/weight:ro \
{IMAGE_ID} bash
```

```bash
export RANKTABLEFILE= {rank_table_file.json path}
```

```bash
cd /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/latest/mindie-service/
```

- Multi-machine: the service configuration on all machines must be consistent; only MIES_CONTAINER_IP is the local machine IP, and rank_table_file.json needs to be configured.

## Installation

Install the NPU driver and firmware: replace `<chip_type>` with the product series, `<version>` with the corresponding version, and `<arch>` with the system architecture, and select the community or commercial version of the corresponding version according to the product series and model.

```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run
```

Set the group and permissions of the weight directory: replace `{/path-to-weights/DeepSeek-V3}` with the actual weight directory.


Start the container: replace `<container-name>` with the container name, replace `{IMAGE_ID}` with the image ID (run `docker images` to view it), and modify the weight mount path according to the actual directory.

```bash

--name <container-name> \

--device=/dev/davinci0:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci1:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci2:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci3:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci_manager:rwm \
--device=/dev/hisi_hdc:rwm \
--device=/dev/devmm_svm:rwm \

-v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi:ro \
-v /usr/local/sbin/:/usr/local/sbin:ro \
-v /home/weight:/home/weight:ro \
{IMAGE_ID} bash
```

```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run
```

```bash
        "ModelDeployConfig" :
        {
            ...
            "ModelConfig" : [
                {
                    ...
                    "modelName" : "DeepSeek-V3.2",                                      # Model name, does not affect service startup
                    "modelWeightPath" : "/mnt/weights/DeepSeek-V3.2-w8a8-mtp-QuaRot",   # Weight path
                    "worldSize" : 16,
                    "cpuMemSize" : 0,
                    "npuMemSize" : -1,
                    "backendType" : "torch",  # Select the inference framework backend; DeepSeek-V3.2 must select torch

                    "tp": 8,                  # Tensor parallelism
                    "cp": 1,                  # Context parallelism
                    "sp": 1,                  # Sequence parallelism

                    ...
                }
            ]
        },
        ...
    },
    ...
}
```

Start the service on both machines at the same time; `Daemon start success!` indicates that the service started successfully.

```bash

cd /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/latest/mindie-service  # Modify according to the actual installation path
./bin/mindieservice_dameon

# If it is the whl package, you can directly execute mindie_llm_server
```

## Verification

After the service starts successfully, send a request: replace `{MASTER_IP}` with the master node IP and `{PORT}` with the port configured in `config.json`.

```bash
curl -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-type: application/json" -X POST -d '{
  "model": "DeepSeek-V3.2",
  "max_tokens": 20,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is deep learning?"}]
}' http://{MASTER_IP}:{PORT}/v1/chat/completions
```

Expected result: a JSON response containing a `choices` field is returned.

Install the NPU driver and firmware: replace `<chip_type>` with the product series, `<version>` with the corresponding version, and `<arch>` with the system architecture, and select the community or commercial version of the corresponding version according to the product series and model.

```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run
```

Start the container: replace `<container-name>` with the container name and `{IMAGE_ID}` with the obtained MindIE image ID.

```bash
--name <container-name> \
-w /home \
--device=/dev/davinci0:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci1:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci2:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci3:rwm \
```

guideMd:
## Prerequisites

- Hardware: inference with W8A8 quantized weights requires at least 4 Atlas 800I A2 (8*64G) inference servers.
- Weights: download the original FP8 weights from the moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Instruct repository on Hugging Face, and reuse the DeepSeek-V2 weight conversion script to complete the conversion on the NPU side.
- Quantization: Kimi-K2 reuses the DeepSeek-V3 model structure, and the W8A8 quantized weights are generated according to the quantization method for DeepSeek models.
- Environment: the host machine must have the NPU driver and firmware installed; the image version must be mindie:2.2 or later, and you need to apply for permission before downloading the image.
- Multi-machine: the service configuration on all machines must be consistent; only MIES_CONTAINER_IP is the local machine address, and rank_table_file.json needs to be configured.

## Installation

Install the NPU driver and firmware: replace `<chip_type>` with the product series, `<version>` with the corresponding version, and `<arch>` with the system architecture, and select the community or commercial version of the corresponding version according to the product series and model.

```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run --full --force
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run --full
```

Configure the weight directory permissions: replace `{/path-to-weights/Kimi-K2-Instruct}` with the actual weight directory, change the group to 1001 and the execution permission to 750.

```sh
chown -R 1001:1001 {/path-to-weights/Kimi-K2-Instruct}
chmod -R 750 {/path-to-weights/Kimi-K2-Instruct}
```

Start the container: replace `<container-name>` with the container name and `{IMAGE_ID}` with the image ID found by `docker images`.

```bash
docker run -it -d --net=host --shm-size=500g \
--name <container-name> \
-w /home \
--device=/dev/davinci0:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci1:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci2:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci3:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci_manager:rwm \
--device=/dev/hisi_hdc:rwm \
--device=/dev/devmm_svm:rwm \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver:ro \
-v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi:ro \
-v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi:ro \
-v /usr/local/sbin/:/usr/local/sbin:ro \
-v /home/weight:/home/weight:ro \
{IMAGE_ID} bash
```

Enter the container: replace `{container name}` with the container name started in the previous step.

```sh
docker exec -it {container name} bash
```

Set the basic environment variables: load the environment variable scripts for CANN, ATB, the model repository, and MindIE in sequence inside the container.

```bash
source /usr/local/Ascend/cann/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/atb-models/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/set_env.sh
```

Enable communication environment variables: `HCCL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` needs to be configured as an integer between 120 and 7200, in seconds; in multi-machine scenarios, set `WORLD_SIZE` to the total number of cards.

```bash
export ATB_LLM_HCCL_ENABLE=1
export ATB_LLM_COMM_BACKEND="hccl"
export HCCL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=7200 # This environment variable needs to be configured as an integer, with a value range of [120,7200], in seconds
Four machines:
export WORLD_SIZE=32
export HCCL_EXEC_TIMEOUT=0
```

Install third-party libraries: Kimi-K2 has specific requirements for the transformers version and blobfile; install according to the versions in the commands.

```bash
# Kimi-K2 has specific transformers version requirements and blobfile third-party library requirements
pip install transformers==4.48.3
pip install blobfile
```

## Deployment

Configure the memory pool extension segment environment variables to enable the virtual memory feature.

```bash
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
```

Set the container address and rank_table_file.json path: replace `{container ip address}` with the local machine address and `{rank_table_file.json path}` with the actual file path; all machines must be consistent except for the local machine address.

```bash
export MIES_CONTAINER_IP={container ip address}
export RANK_TABLE_FILE={rank_table_file.json path}
```

Select the workspace memory allocation algorithm.

```bash
export ATB_WORKSPACE_MEM_ALLOC_ALG_TYPE=3
```

Configure the scheduling and expansion location of the communication algorithm.

```bash
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"
```

Enable HCCL communication and disable the PCIe direct connection restriction.

```bash
export ATB_LLM_HCCL_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_RDMA_PCIE_DIRECT_POST_NOSTRICT=TRUE
```

Enable the asynchronous launch feature.

```bash
export MINDIE_ASYNC_SCHEDULING_ENABLE=1
```

Set core binding.

```bash
export CPU_AFFINITY_CONF=1
```

Enable the queue optimization feature.

```bash
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=2
```

Open the MindIE Service configuration file.

```bash
cd /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/latest/mindie-service/
vim conf/config.json
```

Modify the service parameters: set `httpsEnabled`, `interCommTLSEnabled`, and `interNodeTLSEnabled` to false, fill in `npudeviceIds` with the available NPU IDs, replace `modelWeightPath` with the weight directory, set `worldSize` to 8, and set `multiNodesInferEnabled` to true.

```json
"httpsEnabled" : false, # If the network environment is insecure, HTTPS communication is not enabled; that is, when "httpsEnabled"="false", there is a relatively high network security risk
...
"multiNodesInferEnabled" : true, # Enable multi-machine inference
...
# If security authentication is not required, set the following two parameters to false
"interCommTLSEnabled" : false,
"interNodeTLSEnabled" : false,
...
"npudeviceIds" : [[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]],
...
"modelName" : "kimi_k2" # Does not affect service startup
        "modelWeightPath" : "weight path",
"worldSize":8,
```

Modify the complete configuration example according to the actual environment: change `ipAddress` and `managementIpAddress` to the master node address; `modelName` does not affect service startup; fill in the weight path and dp, tp, moe_ep according to the actual deployment.

```json
{
    "Version" : "1.0.0",

    "ServerConfig" :
    {
        "ipAddress" : "Change to the master node IP",
        "managementIpAddress" : "Change to the master node IP",
        "port" : 1025,
        "managementPort" : 1026,
        "metricsPort" : 1027,
        "allowAllZeroIpListening" : false,
        "maxLinkNum" : 1000,
        "httpsEnabled" : false,
        "fullTextEnabled" : false,
        "tlsCaPath" : "security/ca/",
        "tlsCaFile" : ["ca.pem"],
        "tlsCert" : "security/certs/server.pem",
        "tlsPk" : "security/keys/server.key.pem",
        "tlsCrlPath" : "security/certs/",
        "tlsCrlFiles" : ["server_crl.pem"],
        "managementTlsCaFile" : ["management_ca.pem"],
        "managementTlsCert" : "security/certs/management/server.pem",
        "managementTlsPk" : "security/keys/management/server.key.pem",
        "managementTlsCrlPath" : "security/management/certs/",
        "managementTlsCrlFiles" : ["server_crl.pem"],
        "metricsTlsCaFile" : ["metrics_ca.pem"],
        "metricsTlsCert" : "security/certs/metrics/server.pem",
        "metricsTlsPk" : "security/keys/metrics/server.key.pem",
        "metricsTlsCrlPath" : "security/metrics/certs/",
        "metricsTlsCrlFiles" : ["server_crl.pem"],
        "inferMode" : "standard",
        "interCommTLSEnabled" : false,
        "interCommPort" : 1121,
        "interCommTlsCaPath" : "security/grpc/ca/",
        "interCommTlsCaFiles" : ["ca.pem"],
        "interCommTlsCert" : "security/grpc/certs/server.pem",
        "interCommPk" : "security/grpc/keys/server.key.pem",
        "interCommTlsCrlPath" : "security/grpc/certs/",
        "interCommTlsCrlFiles" : ["server_crl.pem"],
        "openAiSupport" : "vllm",
        "tokenTimeout": 3600,
        "e2eTimeout": 3600,
        "distDPServerEnabled":false
    },

    "BackendConfig" : {
        "backendName" : "mindieservice_llm_engine",
        "modelInstanceNumber" : 1,
        "npuDeviceIds" : [[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]],
```

guideMd:
## Prerequisites

- Hardware: inference using W8A8 quantized weights requires at least 4 Atlas 800I A2 (8*64G) inference servers.
- Weights: download the original FP8 weights from the moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Instruct repository on Hugging Face, and reuse the DeepSeek-V2 conversion script to complete the conversion on the NPU side.
- Quantization: Kimi-K2 reuses the DeepSeek-V3 model structure, and the W8A8 quantized weights are generated according to the quantization method for DeepSeek models.
- Environment: the host machine must have the NPU driver and firmware installed; the image version must be mindie:2.2 or later, and you need to apply for permission before downloading the image.
- Multi-machine: the configuration on all machines must be consistent except for the local machine address, and rank_table_file.json needs to be prepared.

## Installation

Install the NPU driver and firmware: replace `<chip_type>` with the product series, `<version>` with the corresponding version, and `<arch>` with the system architecture, and select the community or commercial version of the corresponding version according to the product series and model.

```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run --full --force
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run --full
```

Configure the weight directory permissions: replace `{/path-to-weights/Kimi-K2-Instruct}` with the actual weight directory, change the group to 1001 and the execution permission to 750.

```sh
chown -R 1001:1001 {/path-to-weights/Kimi-K2-Instruct}
chmod -R 750 {/path-to-weights/Kimi-K2-Instruct}
```

Start the container: replace `<container-name>` with the container name and `{IMAGE_ID}` with the image ID found by `docker images`.

```bash
docker run -it -d --net=host --shm-size=500g \
--name <container-name> \
-w /home \
--device=/dev/davinci0:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci1:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci2:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci3:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci_manager:rwm \
--device=/dev/hisi_hdc:rwm \
--device=/dev/devmm_svm:rwm \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver:ro \
-v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi:ro \
-v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi:ro \
-v /usr/local/sbin/:/usr/local/sbin:ro \
-v /home/weight:/home/weight:ro \
{IMAGE_ID} bash
```

Enter the container: replace `{container name}` with the container name started in the previous step.

```sh
docker exec -it {container name} bash
```

Set the basic environment variables: load the environment variable scripts for CANN, ATB, the model repository, and MindIE in sequence inside the container.

```bash
source /usr/local/Ascend/cann/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/atb-models/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/set_env.sh
```

Enable communication environment variables: `HCCL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` needs to be configured as an integer between 120 and 7200, in seconds; in multi-machine scenarios, set `WORLD_SIZE` to the total number of cards.

```bash
export ATB_LLM_HCCL_ENABLE=1
export ATB_LLM_COMM_BACKEND="hccl"
export HCCL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=7200 # This environment variable needs to be configured as an integer, with a value range of [120,7200], in seconds
Four machines:
export WORLD_SIZE=32
export HCCL_EXEC_TIMEOUT=0
```

Install third-party libraries: Kimi-K2 has specific requirements for the transformers version and blobfile; install according to the versions in the commands.

```bash
# Kimi-K2 has specific transformers version requirements and blobfile third-party library requirements
pip install transformers==4.48.3
pip install blobfile
```

## Deployment

Configure the memory pool extension segment environment variables to enable the virtual memory feature.

```bash
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
```

Set the container address and rank_table_file.json path: replace `{container ip address}` with the local machine address and `{rank_table_file.json path}` with the actual file path; all machines must be consistent except for the local machine address.

```bash
export MIES_CONTAINER_IP={container ip address}
export RANK_TABLE_FILE={rank_table_file.json path}
```

Select the workspace memory allocation algorithm.

```bash
export ATB_WORKSPACE_MEM_ALLOC_ALG_TYPE=3
```

Configure the scheduling and expansion location of the communication algorithm.

```bash
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"
```

Enable HCCL communication and disable the PCIe direct connection restriction.

```bash
export ATB_LLM_HCCL_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_RDMA_PCIE_DIRECT_POST_NOSTRICT=TRUE
```

Enable the asynchronous launch feature.

```bash
export MINDIE_ASYNC_SCHEDULING_ENABLE=1
```

Set core binding.

```bash
export CPU_AFFINITY_CONF=1
```

Enable the queue optimization feature.

```bash
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=2
```

## Prerequisites

- Hardware: 1 Atlas 800I A2 inference server; GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking supports world sizes 1 and 2, and this record is a multi-card parallel deployment.
- Weights: download floating-point weights from the zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking repository on Hugging Face; use the weight version updated after 2025-10-25.
- Quantization: W8A8 quantized weights are generated via `quant_glm4_1v.py` in msmodelslim, with `--w_bit` set to 8, `--a_bit` set to 8, and `--device_type` set to npu.
- Environment: the host machine has the NPU driver and firmware installed; the container image already includes MindIE Service and the model repository, so no separate compilation is needed.
- Path: replace `modelWeightPath` in the configuration file with the quantized weight directory, configure `modelName` as glm4v, and fill in `npuDeviceIds` with the available chip IDs.

## Installation

Install the NPU driver and firmware: replace `<chip_type>` with the product series, `<version>` with the corresponding version, and `<arch>` with the system architecture, and select the community or commercial version of the corresponding version according to the product series and model.

```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run --full --force
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run --full
```

Start the container: replace `<container-name>` with the container name and `{IMAGE_ID}` with the obtained MindIE image ID.

```bash
docker run -it -d --net=host --shm-size=500g \
--name <container-name> \
-w /home \
--device=/dev/davinci0:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci1:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci2:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci3:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci_manager:rwm \
--device=/dev/hisi_hdc:rwm \
--device=/dev/devmm_svm:rwm \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver:ro \
-v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi:ro \
-v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi:ro \
-v /usr/local/sbin/:/usr/local/sbin:ro \
-v /home/weight:/home/weight:ro \
{IMAGE_ID} bash
```

## Deployment

Open the Server configuration file of MindIE Service at `/usr/local/Ascend/mindie/latest/mindie-service/conf/config.json`; adjust the path according to the actual installation location in the image.

```shell
vim /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/latest/mindie-service/conf/config.json
```

Configure the ports, hardware IDs, model name, and weight path: configure `npuDeviceIds` with the available chip IDs of the local machine, replace `modelWeightPath` with the quantized weight directory, configure `modelName` as glm4v, set `worldSize` to the number of parallel cards and make it consistent with the number of chip IDs, set `npuMemSize` to the KV Cache memory allocation for the text model in GB, and `trustRemoteCode` defaults to false.

```json
{
...
"ServerConfig" :
{
...
"httpsEnabled" : false,
...
},

"BackendConfig": {
...
"npuDeviceIds" : [[0,1]], # Chip ID, configure as needed
...
"ModelDeployConfig":
{
"maxSeqLen" : 10240,
"maxInputTokenLen" : 10240,
"truncation" : false,
"ModelConfig" : [
{
"modelInstanceType": "Standard",
"modelName" : "glm4v", # Configure the model name as glm4v
"modelWeightPath" : "/data_mm/weights/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking", # Custom local weight path
"worldSize" : 2, # Number of parallel cards, configure as needed
...
"npuMemSize" : 15, # KV Cache memory allocation for the text model, can be adjusted as needed, in GB
...
"trustRemoteCode" : false # Defaults to false; if set to true, local code is trusted and users need to bear the risk themselves
}
]
}
```

Start the server process: enter the bin directory of mindie-service and execute `./mindieservice_daemon`; the service listens on port 1040 by default.

```shell
cd /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/latest/mindie-service/bin
./mindieservice_daemon
```

```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run
```

```bash
-v /home/weight:/home/weight:ro \
{IMAGE_ID} bash
```

## Prerequisites

- Hardware: 1 Atlas 800I A2 inference server; Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct uses a Dense architecture and supports world sizes 1, 2, 4, and 8, with 2 recommended.
- Weights: download the Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-w8a8-QuaRot quantized weights from ModelScope, or generate W8A8 quantized weights yourself with msmodelslim according to the quantization example.
- Environment: The host has the NPU driver and firmware installed, the Docker version must be 24.x.x or later, and the MindIE image has been obtained.
- Dependencies: install the Python third-party dependencies in the container according to requirements_qwen3vl.txt; for the value of `max_input_length`, refer to `max_position_embeddings` in config.json under the weight directory.
- Path: `weight_path` is the model weight path, `modelWeightPath` in the serving configuration file must point to this directory, and `modelName` is configured as qwen3vl.

## Installation

Install the NPU driver and firmware: replace `<chip_type>` with the product series, `<version>` with the corresponding version, and `<arch>` with the system architecture, and select the community or commercial version of the corresponding version according to the product series and model.

```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run --full --force
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run --full
```

Start the container: replace `<container-name>` with the container name and `{IMAGE_ID}` with the obtained MindIE image ID; `/home/weight` is the mount point of the host weight directory.

```bash
docker run -it -d --net=host --shm-size=500g \
```

- Weights: download floating-point weights from the zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking repository on Hugging Face; use the weight version updated after 2025-10-25.
- Quantization: W8A8 quantized weights are generated via `quant_glm4_1v.py` in msmodelslim, with `--w_bit` set to 8, `--a_bit` set to 8, and `--device_type` set to npu.
- Environment: the host machine has the NPU driver and firmware installed, the Docker version must be 24.x.x or higher, and the inference dependencies are installed according to requirements_glm4v.txt.
- Path: replace `modelWeightPath` with the quantized weight directory, configure `modelName` as glm4v, fill in `npuDeviceIds` with the chip IDs of the local machine, and `worldSize` is the number of parallel cards.

## Installation

Install the NPU driver and firmware: replace `<chip_type>` with the product series, `<version>` with the corresponding version, and `<arch>` with the system architecture, and select the community or commercial version of the corresponding version according to the product series and model.

```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run
```

```bash
-v /usr/local/sbin/:/usr/local/sbin:ro \
```

```shell
vim /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/latest/mindie-service/conf/config.json
```

```json
...
"ServerConfig" :
{
...
"httpsEnabled" : false,

},

...
```

## Prerequisites

- Hardware: 1 Atlas 800I A3 inference server; this record is a single-node deployment, and `worldSize` in the configuration file is consistent with the number of chips used.
- Weights: download floating-point weights from the zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking repository on Hugging Face; use the weight version updated after 2025-10-25.
- Quantization: W8A8 quantized weights are generated via `quant_glm4_1v.py` in msmodelslim, with `--w_bit` set to 8, `--a_bit` set to 8, and `--device_type` set to npu.
- Environment: the host machine has the NPU driver and firmware installed, the Docker version must be 24.x.x or higher, and the inference dependencies are installed according to requirements_glm4v.txt.
- Path: replace `modelWeightPath` with the quantized weight directory, configure `modelName` as glm4v, fill in `npuDeviceIds` with the chip IDs of the local machine, and `worldSize` is the number of parallel cards.

## Installation

Install the NPU driver and firmware: replace `<chip_type>` with the product series, `<version>` with the corresponding version, and `<arch>` with the system architecture, and select the community or commercial version of the corresponding version according to the product series and model.

```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run --full --force
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run --full
```

Start the container: replace `<container-name>` with the container name and `{IMAGE_ID}` with the obtained MindIE image ID; `/home/weight` is the host weight directory.

```bash
docker run -it -d --net=host --shm-size=500g \
--name <container-name> \
-w /home \
--device=/dev/davinci0:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci1:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci2:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci3:rwm \
--device=/dev/davinci_manager:rwm \
--device=/dev/hisi_hdc:rwm \
--device=/dev/devmm_svm:rwm \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver:ro \
-v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi:ro \
-v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi:ro \
-v /usr/local/sbin/:/usr/local/sbin:ro \
-v /home/weight:/home/weight:ro \
{IMAGE_ID} bash
```

## Deployment

Open the server configuration file of MindIE Service, and adjust the path according to the actual installation location in the image.

```shell
vim /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/latest/mindie-service/conf/config.json
```

Configure the ports, hardware IDs, model name, and weight path: configure the chip IDs of `npuDeviceIds` as needed, replace `modelWeightPath` with a custom local weight path, configure `modelName` as glm4v, set `worldSize` to the number of parallel cards as needed, set `npuMemSize` to the KV Cache memory allocation for the text model in GB, and `trustRemoteCode` defaults to false.

```json
{
...
"ServerConfig" :
{
...
"httpsEnabled" : false,
...
},

"BackendConfig": {
...
"npuDeviceIds" : [[0,1]], # Chip ID, configure as needed
...
"ModelDeployConfig":
{
"maxSeqLen" : 10240,
"maxInputTokenLen" : 10240,
"truncation" : false,
"ModelConfig" : [
{
"modelInstanceType": "Standard",
"modelName" : "glm4v", # Configure the model name as glm4v
"modelWeightPath" : "/data_mm/weights/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking", # Custom local weight path
"worldSize" : 2, # Number of parallel cards, configure as needed
...
"npuMemSize" : 15, # KV Cache memory allocation for the text model, can be adjusted as needed, in GB
...
"trustRemoteCode" : false # Defaults to false; if set to true, local code is trusted and users need to bear the risk themselves
}
]
}
```

Start the server process: enter the bin directory of mindie-service and execute `./mindieservice_daemon`; the service listens on port 1040 by default.

```shell
cd /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/latest/mindie-service/bin
./mindieservice_daemon
```
